simple.meaning: גָּרַם (gâram) is a Hebrew action word meaning “(causative) to bone , i.e. denude (by extensive, craunch) the bones.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Numbers, Ezekiel, Zephaniah, beginning at Numbers 24:8. The surrounding contexts include Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּרַם (H1633) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: גָּרַם (gâram) / H1633 is traced through Numbers 24:8, Ezekiel 23:34, Zephaniah 3:3 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: (causative) to bone , i.e. denude (by extensive, craunch) the bones
definitions.full: H1633. garam I. [ גָּרַם ] verb lay aside, leave, save **meaning dubious; ? cut off, hence reserve (Late Hebrew גָּרַם is shorten, occasion, bring about, to pass , Aramaic גְּרַם Pa`el occasion, bring about , abscidit, decrevit , compare also Arabic cut off (fruit), shear (sheep); — on connection of ideas see Fl NHWB i. 437 ) Qal Perfect 3plural לַבֹּקֶר גָָֽרְמוּ לֹא Zeph 3:3 they have left nothing for the morrow , in figure of cruel judges (dubious: al. from II. [ גָּרַם ], see Kau AT Dr). II. [ גָּרַם ] verb denominative break bones, break , — Pi`el Imperfect יְגָרֵם וְעַצְמֹתֵיהֶם Num 24:8 (JE); but also תְּגָרֵ֖מִי וְאֶתחֲֿרָשֶׂיהָ Ezek 23:34 (yet on text see Co.)
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root; to be spare or skeleton-like; used only as a denominative from 1634 ;

occurrences.englishText: God brings him out of Egypt.
You will even drink it and drain it out.
Her princes within her are roaring lions. Her judges are evening wolves. They leave nothing until the next day.
